Work ONLY inside /opt/nxeon-wt-capacity (a pre-created git worktree, branch `feature/freemc-capacity`, off the Nxeon hosting platform's main repo). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or any other /opt/nxeon-wt-* directory — other work may be happening concurrently. `node_modules` and `.env` in your worktree are symlinks to the main repo (normal) — but NEVER run `git add -A`, it's a known hazard that can corrupt the main repo's real `node_modules` through the symlink. Only ever `git add` the exact file paths you changed.

This is a real production hosting business (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). Free Minecraft hosting product: customers get a personal Minecraft server as a Docker container on a shared host called `freemc-host`. Each container auto-sleeps when empty and wakes on connection (via `mc-router`, a third-party Go proxy that watches for incoming connections and runs `docker start` on the target container itself — it acts autonomously, outside this app's control, for that specific wake path).

## Real capacity numbers, just confirmed live on the host

- `freemc-host`: 7.8GB RAM, **only 3 vCPUs**.
- In `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`, `recreateGameTypeContainer` already assigns `cpus = kind === "plugins" ? 2 : 1` and (as of a fix earlier today) `ramMb = kind === "plugins" ? Math.max(params.ramMb, 2560) : params.ramMb`.
- Do the math: this host can run at most ONE plugin-kind server (2 of 3 vCPUs) plus one lightweight vanilla-kind server (1 vCPU) awake at the same time before CPU oversubscription — regardless of RAM headroom. CPU is the binding constraint, not RAM.
- Only one free MC server exists in the whole system today (early test phase), so this hasn't caused a customer-visible problem yet — but it will as soon as a second or third customer's server is awake at the same time as an existing one, especially if more than one is plugin-kind (SkyBlock, Prison, Towny, Parkour, Anarchy, Lifesteal, MissileWars, SurvivalGames are all `kind:"plugins"`; only the base Vanilla Survival type is `kind:"properties"`).

## What to build (three pieces, deliberately kept small — NOT a queue system)

### 1. A shared capacity-accounting helper

Add a function (in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` or a new small file like `lib/freemc-capacity.ts` — your call, but prefer co-locating with the existing `docker ps`/`docker inspect` patterns already in `free-minecraft-control.ts` if that keeps it simple) that, given the SSH `conn` to `freemc-host`, returns something like:

```ts
type FreemcHostCapacity = {
  totalCpus: number;        // from `nproc` or a config constant — check live, don't hardcode blindly
  totalRamMb: number;       // from `free -m` or similar
  committedCpus: number;    // sum of --cpus across all RUNNING (not stopped/exited) free-mc containers
  committedRamMb: number;   // sum of assigned memory limits across all running free-mc containers
  runningContainers: Array<{ containerName: string; cpus: number; ramMb: number; startedAt: string }>;
};
```

Determine "which containers are free-mc containers" the same way the rest of this file already does (they're named `mc-free-<userId>` per the existing `containerName` convention — check `db.freeMinecraftServer` for the naming pattern, or just filter `docker ps` output by the `mc-free-` prefix, matching how `mc-router` and existing code already reason about these containers). Get each running container's actual assigned CPU/RAM via `docker inspect <name> --format '{{.HostConfig.NanoCpus}} {{.HostConfig.Memory}}'` (same fields already used elsewhere in this file — search for `NanoCpus`/`.HostConfig.Memory` for the existing pattern).

Live-test this against the real host to make sure the numbers come back sane (there's currently one container that may be running or stopped — check `docker ps -a` first to know what state to expect).

### 2. Gate dashboard-triggered starts with it

Find where a customer explicitly triggers a container start from OUR OWN app code (NOT the passive mc-router wake path) — likely `recreateGameTypeContainer` itself, or whatever calls it from `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts` / `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` when a customer creates a server, switches game type, or manually starts a sleeping one from the dashboard. Before proceeding with the `docker run`, call the capacity helper and check: would adding this container's `cpus`/`ramMb` push `committedCpus`/`committedRamMb` past `totalCpus`/`totalRamMb` (leave a small safety margin, e.g. don't use the literal 100% — maybe reserve 1 CPU and ~1GB for the OS/Docker daemon itself, check what's realistic against the live host's actual idle baseline usage)? If so, return a clear, honest error like `{ ok: false, error: "Free servers are at capacity right now — try again in a few minutes." }` instead of proceeding into a start that would likely crash or starve an existing customer's running server.

Do NOT touch or attempt to gate the mc-router passive-wake path — that's out of scope for this task (mc-router acts autonomously and isn't something this codebase controls). Just gate the paths we do control.

### 3. Admin-facing resource-usage meters

Add a resource-usage view to the ADMIN free-Minecraft panel — check `app/admin/free-minecraft/page.tsx` and `components/admin/FreeMinecraftControls.tsx` for the existing admin surface and its styling conventions (Nxeon navy/violet/cyan theme — match whatever's already there, don't introduce a new visual language). Show:
- Host-level totals: CPU committed/total, RAM committed/total, as simple meters/bars (percentage-based, with a warning color state — check if this codebase already has a semantic warning/critical color convention used elsewhere in the admin panel, e.g. for the node-RAM-tuning or backup-status work, and reuse it rather than inventing a new one).
- Per-running-container breakdown: container name (or better, resolve back to the owning customer/game-type via `db.freeMinecraftServer` so an admin sees something meaningful, not just a raw container name), assigned CPU/RAM, and how long it's been running.

This should be a new server action (e.g. `getFreemcHostCapacity` in `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, following whatever pattern the existing admin freemc actions use) plus whatever UI wiring is needed. It's fine for this to be a simple polling refresh (a button, or refresh-on-tab-focus) rather than a live websocket — this is an admin diagnostic view, not a customer-facing real-time feature.

## Constraints — important

- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-capacity` before finishing.
- Live-test the capacity-accounting math against the real host (SSH pattern: `const host = await db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" }, select: { id:true, rootPassword:true, rootPasswordEnc:true, sshPort:true, dedicatedIp:{select:{address:true}} } }); await withServerSsh(host!, async (conn) => { ... });` from `./lib/db` and `./lib/ssh-exec`, run via `npx tsx -e "..."` from inside the worktree) — don't just trust the code compiles, confirm the numbers it reports match what `docker ps`/`docker inspect`/`free -m` actually show on the real host.
- Commit with a clear message. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging, do NOT run deploy/promote scripts — a human handles integration and production deployment separately, on purpose.
- Report back: the exact capacity math/thresholds you used and why, what you found live on the host, the files touched, and confirm you committed on `feature/freemc-capacity`.

1	/**
2	 * Docker/RCON control primitives for free-tier Minecraft containers on
3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);
63	    const p = parsed?.server_info?.players;
64	    if (typeof p?.online === "number" && typeof p?.max === "number") {
65	      return { running: true, players: { online: p.online, max: p.max } };
66	    }
67	  } catch {
68	    /* fall through */
69	  }
70	  return { running: true, players: null };
71	}
72	
73	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
74	
75	// Some plugins (EssentialsX's /list override is the one that's bitten us)
76	// colorize their command output with raw ANSI escape codes, which the RCON
77	// protocol passes straight through as literal bytes in the response text —
78	// there's no terminal on the other end to interpret them. Confirmed live: a
79	// player name came back as "papiguapo\x1b[0m", which then failed every
80	// caller's name validation (it's not alphanumeric) and broke the inventory
81	// editor's "pick a valid player" check even with a real player selected.
82	// Stripped once here so every RCON consumer (players list, Console tab,
83	// Roles, inventory editor) gets clean text for free.
84	const ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g;

86	/** One RCON round-trip via the bundled rcon-cli — see lib/game-control.ts's
87	 *  validateRconCommand for the same input sanitation used on the paid path. */
88	export async function sendRcon(
89	  conn: Client,
90	  containerName: string,
91	  ownerId: string,
92	  command: string,
93	): Promise<RconResult> {
94	  const password = rconPasswordFor(ownerId);
95	  const r = await dockerExec(
96	    conn,
97	    containerName,
98	    `env RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(password)} rcon-cli ${shellQuote(command)}`,
99	    12_000,
100	  );
101	  if (r.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: r.stderr.trim() || "RCON command failed." };
102	  return { ok: true, response: r.stdout.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, "").trim() };
103	}

107	/** Parses rcon-cli's `list` response: "There are N of a max of M players online: a, b, c" */
108	export async function getFreeServerPlayers(
109	  conn: Client,
110	  containerName: string,
111	  ownerId: string,
112	): Promise<{ ok: true; players: PlayerInfo[] } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
113	  const r = await sendRcon(conn, containerName, ownerId, "list");
114	  if (!r.ok) return r;
115	  const colonIdx = r.response.indexOf(":");
116	  if (colonIdx === -1) return { ok: true, players: [] };
117	  const names = r.response
118	    .slice(colonIdx + 1)
119	    .split(",")
120	    .map((s) => s.trim())
121	    .filter(Boolean);
122	  return { ok: true, players: names.map((name) => ({ name })) };
123	}

125	/** Reads /data/server.properties into a plain key->value map. */
126	export async function readServerProperties(
127	  conn: Client,
128	  containerName: string,
129	): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
130	  const r = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, "cat /data/server.properties", 10_000);
131	  if (r.code !== 0) return {};
132	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
133	  for (const line of r.stdout.split("\n")) {
134	    if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
135	    const i = line.indexOf("=");
136	    if (i === -1) continue;
137	    out[line.slice(0, i).trim()] = line.slice(i + 1).trim();
138	  }
139	  return out;
140	}

142	/**
143	 * Writes a set of server.properties keys in place (sed-style line replace,
144	 * appending any key not already present) and restarts the container so the
145	 * itzg entrypoint's normal boot sequence picks the new values up — the image
146	 * only reads server.properties at startup (confirmed against the Minecraft
147	 * wiki: none of gamemode/motd/max-players/etc. persist a live RCON change back
148	 * to the file), so a restart is the only fully-reliable way to apply anything
149	 * here. Keys with a real live RCON equivalent (difficulty, whitelist on/off)
150	 * are ALSO pushed live by the caller for instant effect — see FIELD_LIVE_CMD.
151	 */
152	export async function writeServerProperties(
153	  conn: Client,
154	  containerName: string,
155	  changes: Record<string, string>,
156	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
157	  const current = await readServerProperties(conn, containerName);
158	  const merged = { ...current, ...changes };
159	  const body = Object.entries(merged)
160	    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)
161	    .join("\n");
162	  const write = await execInput(
163	    conn,
164	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c 'cat > /data/server.properties'`,
165	    body + "\n",
166	    10_000,
167	  );
168	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write server.properties." };
169	  return { ok: true };
170	}

744	  conn: Client,
745	  containerName: string,
746	  message: string,

748	  const path = "/data/plugins/Essentials/config.yml";
749	  const read = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, `cat ${path}`, 10_000);
750	  if (read.code !== 0) {

763	    patched,

772	/**
773	 * Polls until the Minecraft server inside `containerName` has actually
774	 * finished booting (its log prints "Done (Ns)!") or gives up.
775	 *
776	 * This exists because BOTH of the "is it ready" checks it replaces were too
777	 * shallow: `docker inspect ...State.Running` only proves the container
778	 * PROCESS hasn't crashed — a plugin-heavy boot spends 40-90s downloading and
779	 * loading before the game itself is reachable, and that whole window used to
780	 * read as "ready". Worse, mc-router's own wake check has the identical gap:
781	 * it just opens a raw TCP connection to :25565, and Minecraft's listener
782	 * binds early, well before world/plugin loading finishes — so the port looks
783	 * "up" long before the server can actually complete a client handshake. Both
784	 * gaps together are exactly what produced a real, reproduced-live customer
785	 * bug: switching to SkyBlock reported success, mc-router's TCP check passed
786	 * within seconds, and the customer's client still got "Failed to connect —
787	 * Timed out" because the server was still mid-boot. Polling the log line
788	 * itself is the only signal that means what it says.
789	 *
790	 * `docker restart` re-runs the exact same boot sequence as a fresh `docker
791	 * run`, so this same wait is needed after `applyModeProperties`'s restart
792	 * too, not just the initial container creation.
793	 */
794	async function waitForServerReady(
795	  conn: Client,
796	  containerName: string,
797	  timeoutMs = 110_000,
798	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
799	  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
800	  // First few seconds are the container just starting up (image entrypoint,
801	  // ownership fix, etc.) — no point polling logs before that's underway.
802	  await sleep(3_000);
803	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
804	    const running = await exec(conn, `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`, 10_000);
805	    if (running.code !== 0 || running.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
806	      return { ok: false, error: "Container exited before finishing startup." };
807	    }
808	    const logs = await exec(conn, `docker logs ${shellQuote(containerName)} --tail 200 2>&1`, 10_000);
809	    if (/\bDone \([\d.]+s\)!/.test(logs.stdout)) return { ok: true };
810	    await sleep(3_000);
811	  }
812	  return { ok: false, error: "Server took too long to start." };
813	}

817	 * GAME MODE applied on top (see mergeGameTypeAndMode) — the single shared
818	 * implementation every game-type-switching action (lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts,
819	 * lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts) builds its `docker run` from, so the LEVEL /
820	 * mode-controlled-key handling below can't drift between call sites the way
821	 * three independently hand-rolled `docker run` commands eventually would.
822	 *

824	 * `<LEVEL>`/`<LEVEL>_nether`/`<LEVEL>_the_end` folder set inside the SAME

826	 * live — see the module-doc note above FREEMC_GAME_TYPES). Deliberately does
827	 * NOT env-bake gamemode/hardcore/difficulty (see envForGameType) — those are
828	 * applied in a second pass via applyModeProperties, once the container is
829	 * confirmed alive, so a later mode-only restart can always change them
830	 * cleanly without a recreate.
831	 *
832	 * Verifies liveness twice — once ~15s after `docker run` (long enough for an
833	 * init-time plugin/version failure to have already killed it), once more
834	 * ~8s after the follow-up mode-properties restart — and never throws; the
835	 * caller decides what a failure means (typically: roll back to the
836	 * account's previous type/mode).

838	export async function recreateGameTypeContainer(
839	  conn: Client,
840	  params: {
841	    containerName: string;
842	    dataPath: string;
843	    subdomain: string;
844	    domain: string;
845	    ramMb: number;
846	    ownerId: string;
847	    gameType: FreeMcGameType;
848	    gameTypeKey: string;
849	    gameMode: FreeMcGameMode;
850	    /** Extra env vars layered on top of the type's own (e.g. the Mod Menu's
851	     *  merged MODRINTH_PROJECTS list) — last-write-wins over the type's env. */
852	    extraEnv?: Record<string, string>;
853	  },
854	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
855	  const jvmRatio = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 0.7 : 0.85; // plugins need more non-heap headroom — see FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION's neighboring history
856	  const cpus = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 2 : 1; // see recreatePresetContainer's note on mc-router's fixed 60s wake timeout
857	  // The global free_minecraft_ram_mb setting (1024 by default) is sized for
858	  // the properties-only presets — plugins-kind ones (EssentialsX + LuckPerms
859	  // + Vault + a type's own plugins, up to 6 loaded dimensions on something
860	  // like SkyBlock) run noticeably heavier and were found live to OOM-kill a
861	  // short while AFTER printing "Done" at that ceiling — not during boot, so
862	  // the old shallow "still alive 15s after docker run" check never caught it,
863	  // and the fix wasn't the plugins themselves (confirmed by re-testing with
864	  // WorldEdit removed — same crash, same timing) or --cpus. It really is a
865	  // sizing problem: 1536m/0.7 ran the same SkyBlock config stable for 100s+
866	  // post-boot with ONE player — but confirmed live it's still not enough
867	  // once a SECOND player joins: memory climbed to 90% (1.355GB/1.5GB) during
868	  // the second player's own island-creation schematic paste (world-gen +
869	  // chunk load + plugin bookkeeping for two islands across up to 6
870	  // dimensions at once), and the container was killed twice in that window
871	  // before settling. 2560m/0.7 gives real headroom for that case; the free
872	  // tier is a shared/social product, so "two friends on one server" is the
873	  // common case, not an edge case. Bump container memory for plugin-kind
874	  // presets specifically rather than raising the global default (which
875	  // properties-only presets don't need).
876	  const ramMb = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? Math.max(params.ramMb, 2560) : params.ramMb;
877	  const jvmMb = Math.max(256, Math.round(ramMb * jvmRatio));
878	
879	  const envVars = { ...envForGameType(params.gameType), ...(params.extraEnv ?? {}), LEVEL: params.gameTypeKey };
880	  const envFlags = Object.entries(envVars)
881	    .map(([k, v]) => `-e ${k}=${shellQuote(v)}`)
882	    .join(" ");
883	
884	  await exec(conn, `docker rm -f ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`, 30_000);
885	  const cmd = [
886	    "docker run -d",
887	    `--name ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`,
888	    "--network freemc",
889	    `--memory=${ramMb}m --memory-swap=${ramMb}m --cpus=${cpus}`,
890	    `--label mc-router.host=${shellQuote(`${params.subdomain}.${params.domain}`)}`,
891	    `-v ${shellQuote(params.dataPath)}:/data`,
892	    `-e EULA=TRUE -e TYPE=${params.gameType.type ?? "VANILLA"} -e ONLINE_MODE=FALSE`,
893	    params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? `-e VERSION=${shellQuote(FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION)}` : "",
894	    `-e MEMORY=${jvmMb}m`,
895	    `-e ENABLE_RCON=true -e RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(rconPasswordFor(params.ownerId))}`,
896	    envFlags,
897	    "itzg/minecraft-server",
898	  ].join(" ");
899	  const run = await exec(conn, cmd, 90_000); // plugin downloads can take longer than a plain boot
900	  if (run.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: run.stderr || "docker run failed" };
901	
902	  const ready = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName);
903	  if (!ready.ok) return ready;
904	
905	  // IridiumSkyblock ships with `islandCreateOnJoin: false` — a customer who
906	  // joins fresh just spawns in the plain overworld terrain (which, since
907	  // that's Paper's stock generator, looks exactly like Vanilla), with no
908	  // floating island and no indication one exists to create. Confirmed live:
909	  // a customer reported "joined the server but it has vanilla loaded even
910	  // though I chose skyblock" — this is why. The config file only exists
911	  // after the plugin's first boot (it writes its own defaults), so this has
912	  // to run as a post-boot patch, not something bakeable into the image/env.
913	  // Patched HERE — right after the first readiness wait, BEFORE
914	  // applyModeProperties's own restart below — so that ONE restart picks up
915	  // both this and the mode properties together. An earlier version patched
916	  // this AFTER applyModeProperties with its own separate restart+wait, which
917	  // meant a SkyBlock switch chained three full boot-and-wait cycles back to
918	  // back (each 40-90s) — confirmed live to run past whatever the browser/
919	  // client was willing to wait for, so the switch would actually succeed
920	  // server-side a couple minutes later while the customer had already seen
921	  // a timeout/error and given up. Two cycles instead of three meaningfully
922	  // shortens that window; a config patch with no plugin process running yet
923	  // to pick it up costs nothing extra by itself.
924	  //
925	  // `islandCreateOnJoin` alone was not the whole bug: it only makes the
926	  // plugin create the island in the background. Whether the player actually
927	  // gets TELEPORTED there is a separate key, `spawnOnIsland`, which also
928	  // ships `false` — so even with an island silently created, the player was
929	  // left standing in that same plain default-generator "skyblock" level,
930	  // which is exactly the "shows active on skyblock but loads vanilla world"
931	  // report. Both keys have to be true for a fresh join to actually land the
932	  // player on their island.

935	  // stack never installs WorldEdit (the boot log warns "selected paster
936	  // [worldedit] is not available, available choices are [internalAsync]"),

**Reservation chosen: 1 vCPU + 1024MB**, per the task's suggested figures — but I checked the live idle baseline first rather than accepting them blindly: with everything but `mc-router` stopped, the host showed ~0% CPU busy and only ~592MB RAM used (rest is reclaimable buff/cache). So idle overhead alone would justify a much smaller margin; the full 1 vCPU/1GB is a deliberate conservative buffer for bursty load (plugin downloads, log rotation, cron, an admin's own SSH/inspect session) rather than a measured minimum. One consequence worth flagging: this margin is tight enough that the "1 plugin-kind (2 vCPU) + 1 vanilla-kind (1 vCPU)" combo described in the task brief as the theoretical max *doesn't* clear the margined budget (2+1=3 > budget of 2) — the margined host can run one plugin-kind server alone, or up to two vanilla-kind together, but not both kinds at once.
